content: 1. Omeprazole reduces the effectiveness of cefpodoxime by increasing gastric pH, which affects the drug's solubility and absorption. This interaction is relevant only when both drugs are administered orally. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Clarithromycin decreases the effectiveness of cefuroxime through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor the patient closely when these drugs are co-administered. 3. Omeprazole reduces the effectiveness of cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH, impacting its solubility and absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Cenobamate increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2C19, which is involved in omeprazole metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 5. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 6. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 7. When cenobamate is co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates, consider increasing the dose of the substrate as needed. Monitor the patient closely. 8. Clarithromycin increases ceritinib levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is significant and requires the use of alternative drugs. 9. Both ceritinib and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 10. Clarithromycin increases ceritinib levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Omeprazole reduces ceritinib effectiveness by increasing gastric pH, which decreases ceritinib solubility and bioavailability. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cevimeline by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Omeprazole also increases chlordiazepoxide levels by reducing its metabolism. These interactions are minor, but their clinical significance is unknown. 14. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 15. Clarithromycin increases chloroquine levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 16. Both chlorpromazine and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 17. Clarithromycin reduces the effectiveness of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration of systemic antibiotics with the cholera vaccine, as they may inactivate the vaccine strain. Do not administer the vaccine to patients who have received antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 18. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of cholic acid by reducing its elimination. Avoid concomitant use of bile salt efflux pump (BSEP) inhibitors, as they may exacerbate the accumulation of conjugated bile salts in the liver, leading to clinical symptoms. If co-administration is necessary, monitor serum transaminases and bilirubin levels closely. 19. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ciclesonide (inhaled) by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Clarithromycin also increases cilostazol levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Clarithromycin increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Cimetidine also increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Clarithromycin increases cinacalcet levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. Omeprazole decreases ciprofloxacin levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Both clarithromycin and ciprofloxacin prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 25. Both clarithromycin and cisapride prolong the QTc interval, significantly increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Co-administration is contraindicated. 26. Omeprazole increases citalopram levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Both clarithromycin and citalopram prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Monitor QT interval or ECG for signs of QT/QTc prolongation or ventricular tachyarrhythmias. 28. Clarithromycin increases clevidipine levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as increased calcium channel blocker effects may lead to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. 29. Omeprazole increases clobazam levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Dosage adjustment may be required, as CYP2C19 inhibitors can increase exposure to N-desmethylclobazam (active metabolite). Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Both clarithromycin and clofazimine prolong the QTc interval, significantly increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Co-administration is contraindicated. 31. Omeprazole increases clomipramine levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Clarithromycin also increases clomipramine levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 32. Clarithromycin increases clonazepam levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Omeprazole also increases clonazepam levels by reducing its metabolism. These interactions are minor, but their clinical significance is unknown. 33. Omeprazole reduces clopidogrel effectiveness by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism, which is essential for clopidogrel bioactivation. Clarithromycin also reduces clopidogrel levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 34. Clarithromycin increases clorazepate levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Omeprazole also increases clorazepate levels by reducing its metabolism. These interactions are minor, but their clinical significance is unknown. 35. Clarithromycin increases clozapine levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 36. Cobicistat increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Clarithromycin also increases cobicistat levels through the same mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 37. Clarithromycin increases cobimetinib levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 38. Clarithromycin increases colchicine levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid use with drugs that are both P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If co-administration is necessary, reduce colchicine dose or frequency as recommended. Co-administration is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 39. Clarithromycin increases conivaptan levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 40. Omeprazole increases conivaptan levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 41. Clarithromycin increases conjugated estrogen levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Clarithromycin increases copanlisib levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 43. Clarithromycin increases cortisone levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Omeprazole reduces crizotinib effectiveness by increasing gastric pH, which decreases crizotinib solubility and bioavailability. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Clarithromycin increases crizotinib levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 46. Both clarithromycin and crizotinib prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 47. Crofelemer increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Omeprazole reduces cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Its clinical significance is unknown. 49. Cyclophosphamide increases clarithromycin and omeprazole levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions are minor, and their clinical significance is unknown. 50. Omeprazole and cyclosporine may increase each other's toxicity through unspecified mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Clarithromycin increases cyclosporine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 52. Clarithromycin increases dabigatran levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration in patients with atrial fibrillation if CrCl <30 mL/min or in patients with DVT/PE if CrCl <50 mL/min. 53. Dabrafenib decreases omeprazole levels by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 54. Omeprazole reduces dabrafenib effectiveness by increasing gastric pH, which decreases dabrafenib solubility and bioavailability. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Clarithromycin increases dabrafenib levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 56. Omeprazole increases dacomitinib levels through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid PPIs with dacomitinib; consider using locally-acting antacids or H2-receptor antagonists instead. 57. Clarithromycin increases dalteparin effects by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 58. Danazol increases omeprazole and clarithromycin levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions are minor, and their clinical significance is unknown. 59. Clarithromycin increases dapsone levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Clarithromycin increases daridorexant levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 61. Darifenacin decreases omeprazole levels through unspecified mechanisms. Its clinical significance is unknown. Darifenacin also increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
